title: ContactsBackend::update_object doc does not specify patch format (RFC 7396 merge vs RFC 6901 JSON Pointer)
description:
LOCATION: crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/backend.rs:51-65

DOC:
    /// Apply a partial update (patch) to an existing AddressBook or
    /// ContactCard.
    ///
    /// Returns `Some(updated_object)` if the backend modified any
    /// properties beyond what the client requested (RFC 8620 §5.3
    /// server-set field echo), or `None` if the patch was applied
    /// verbatim. Per-request auth context is available via the `caller`
    /// parameter, which the `register_contacts_handlers` closures
    /// forward unchanged from [`jmap_server::Dispatcher::dispatch`].
    fn update_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(
        &self,
        caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
        id: &jmap_types::Id,
        patch: O::Patch,
    ) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Result<Option<O>, BackendSetError<Self::Error>>> + Send;

PROBLEM:
The `patch: O::Patch` parameter has an undocumented format contract.
RFC 8620 §5.3 specifies that JMAP `/set update` uses a "PatchObject"
where keys are JSON Pointer paths (RFC 6901) — keys may contain `/`
for nested updates, `~0` for `~`, `~1` for `/`. The reference impl at
memory.rs:677 applies the patch via `jmap_server::json_merge_patch`,
which is RFC 7396 (Merge Patch). These two semantics DIVERGE:

- **JSON Pointer (RFC 8620 §5.3, RFC 6901):** key "addressBookIds/ab1"
  means "set the ab1 field inside addressBookIds". Setting a path to
  null DELETES the leaf.
- **Merge Patch (RFC 7396):** key "addressBookIds/ab1" is a literal
  top-level field name. Setting a field to null DELETES the top-level
  field.

A backend implementor reading the trait doc has no way to know which
semantics they must implement. The PatchObject type (defined in
jmap-types) is a `Map<String, serde_json::Value>` — opaque shape.

EVIDENCE FROM REFERENCE IMPL:
crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/memory.rs:677
    if let Err(MergePatchError::DepthExceeded) = json_merge_patch(&mut current, patch_val) {

uses RFC 7396 merge semantics. The handler at addressbook.rs:195
deserializes the wire-format Value into a `PatchObject` via serde —
which preserves the dotted/slashed key form but does NOT split or
apply the pointer.

THIS DIVERGES FROM RFC 8620 §5.3.

A backend impl that correctly implements RFC 8620 §5.3 JSON Pointer
semantics will produce DIFFERENT results from the MemoryBackend
reference impl on patches containing "/" in keys. Round-tripping a
JMAP wire-format /set call through different backends yields
divergent state. JMAP-qz9v.10 / JMAP-qz9v.4 from the parent epic touch
on the same concern from the apply_jmap_patch helper angle; the
TRAIT-LEVEL angle is that the patch-format contract is unspecified at
the API boundary.

WHAT CALLERS CANNOT DEPEND ON:
- That a backend's update_object behaves the same as the reference impl
  on the same wire input.
- That a deeply-nested patch like {"addressBookIds/ab1": null} applied
  by the backend matches RFC 8620 §5.3 expectations.
- That null-valued patch keys delete the field rather than overwrite
  with null.

RECOMMENDED:
Document at the trait-method level which patch semantics the backend
MUST implement, and reference RFC 8620 §5.3. Add either:
(a) "The backend MUST apply `patch` as an RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch.
    The handler is responsible for converting RFC 8620 §5.3 JSON-Pointer-
    keyed wire values into a flat merge-patch shape before calling this
    method." — and update the handler to do that conversion (today it
    does not; PatchObject keys are forwarded as-is).
(b) "The backend MUST apply `patch` as an RFC 8620 §5.3 PatchObject:
    keys are JSON Pointer paths (RFC 6901); null values delete the
    leaf; intermediate objects are created on demand." — and update
    the MemoryBackend reference impl to use a pointer-aware apply
    helper (consolidating with the apply_jmap_patch helper from
    card.rs that JMAP-qz9v.10 flags).

Workspace canonical-template propagation rule: same gap exists in
jmap-mail-server. Decide which semantics rule, fix the canonical, then
sweep the siblings.
close_reason: Landed on main as 9e113188 (docs(servers): specify update_object patch format). Review passed; integration CI green.
